children: The trade balance rose to €14.2bn, up from €7.3bn in June and €10.7bn a year earlier, Eurostat reported.
This was the highest since October 2025 and well above the €3.7bn expected by economists.

"The increase was mainly driven by a higher surplus in chemicals and related products, in other manufactured goods and food and drink, partially offset by a decrease of surplus in machinery and vehicles," Eurostat said.
Exports were 9% higher than the year before at €276bn, a 16-month high, while imports were up 7.9% year-on-year at €261.8bn.
